frame: Be-ellipsis after ", but": clause 1 "Renters younger than sixty-five are eligible ... if a landlord has registered the unit" holds both the be-predicate and a competing singular perfect in its condition; clause 2 "the elderly in its hill districts" + the blank
decider_quote: Renters younger than sixty-five are eligible
deletion_test: Delete the main predicate "are eligible": the only auxiliary left in the sentence is "has registered", which belongs to the landlord condition; nothing chooses be over have, and the other sentences ("reviewed", "found", "suspect") are not antecedents of this ellipsis.

distractor_pulls.has not: "has registered" is the finite verb nearest the blank and is singular; a reader who matches the ellipsis to the closest auxiliary, and reads "the elderly" as a singular group label, writes "has not".
distractor_pulls.is not: "the elderly" carries no plural -s and is often treated as a mass noun ("the elderly population"); the singular "landlord" and "unit" in the same sentence reinforce a singular reading.
distractor_pulls.have not: Right number, and "have" copies the perfect auxiliary of "has registered", the only auxiliary in the sentence; "but X have not" is also the default negative tag in speech.

distractor_kills.has not: Ellipsis repeats the auxiliary of the parallel main predicate ("are eligible"), and "the + adjective" for people is plural. Correct in: "A landlord has registered the unit, but the tenant has not."
distractor_kills.is not: "the elderly" naming a class of people is plural. Correct in: "The unit is eligible, but the garage is not."
distractor_kills.have not: "have not" would elide "have registered the unit", which is the landlord's action, not a predicate contrasted with "Renters ... are eligible"; parallel ellipsis needs "are". Correct in: "Landlords have registered their units, but tenants have not."

heuristics_that_give_key: proximity reader: 'districts' pl agrees (row-fixed Near pl)
hostile_reader.changed: Revision: new architecture. The be-predicate is now ~22 words back and a competing singular perfect ("if a landlord has registered") sits between it and the blank, so 'copy the first clause's verb' no longer has one candidate; new topic.

frame: Clause 1 ends with the plural owner "infants" before a semicolon; clause 2 opens with a fronted locative "behind a one-way mirror," then the singular subject "an eye tracker" + the blank
deletion_test: Delete "for seated infants": nothing in the passage owns eyes (puppets are props, the first sentence names no person), so its/their is unsettled.

distractor_pulls.follow their: "their" is right, and the plural verb matches the plural noun it points to; the plural cast of the sentence ("trials", "two puppets", "infants") keeps the reader in the plural.
distractor_pulls.follows its: The verb is right, and "its" copies the singular subject or the singular "mirror" right before it; "a tracker follows its ..." sounds like a device and its own target.
distractor_pulls.follow its: "follow" is pulled by the plural "puppets act out" of the parallel first clause (same present tense); "its" by "mirror" and "tracker" next to the blank.

distractor_kills.follow their: Subject-verb: the subject is the singular "tracker"; the fronted phrase is not the subject. Correct in: "two eye trackers follow their eyes".
distractor_kills.follows its: Pronoun-antecedent: eyes belong to the infants; a tracker and a mirror have none. Correct in: "the tracker follows its calibration routine".
distractor_kills.follow its: Wrong on both. Correct in: "the trackers follow its eyes" after a single infant.

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: Key uniquely longest (13 vs 10-12); my one allowed case.
heuristics_that_give_key: (f) opposite verb/pronoun numbers: YES - table-level tell shared by every pronoun slot; I cannot remove it without changing the row
hostile_reader.changed: Revision: fronted locative before the subject; possessed noun changed to one that the singular nouns cannot own at all ("eyes"); verb changed.

frame: Colon after "a dispute that had divided the valley"; direct question with fronted wh-object and inverted "should", ending on the transitive verb "teach"; next sentence opens "Most parents favored ..."
structure: Left: "which language should the merged school teach" (direct question, auxiliary before subject). Right: "Most parents favored offering both" (independent clause). With no mark, "teach most parents" reads as verb + object until "favored".

distractor_pulls.teach. Most: The question is not introduced as a question ("inherited a dispute ...:"), so it reads as a reported matter inside a statement, which ends with a period.
distractor_pulls.teach, most: A reader who takes the colon's content as a reported issue continues with a comma into a result clause ("..., most parents favored ..."), as in a long declarative sentence.
distractor_pulls.teach most: "teach most parents" is a natural verb + object phrase (a school teaching parents), so the run-on parses smoothly for several words until "favored".

distractor_kills.teach. Most: A direct question (inverted "should") ends with a question mark. Correct in: "...: which language the merged school should teach. Most ..." (statement order).
distractor_kills.teach, most: Comma splice: two independent clauses joined by a comma alone.
distractor_kills.teach most: Fused sentence: "most parents favored ..." has its own subject and verb, and "favored" leaves no role for "most parents" as an object of "teach".

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: Two capitalized, two lower-case; no odd one out.
heuristics_that_give_key: noticing the inversion gives the key (row-fixed: the question must be direct)
hostile_reader.changed: Revision: removed "put a single question to parents" (which announced the question); the question now ends on a transitive verb so the no-mark option garden-paths ("teach most parents"); new opening sentence architecture (when-clause + colon), new words before/after the blank.

frame: Fronted if-clause with a past verb ("If outdated forms reached the front desk during the filing season,") BEFORE the subject; plural head "applications" + "from the county's largest employer" + the blank; nothing after the blank decides anything
decider_quote: If outdated forms reached the front desk during the filing season
deletion_test: Delete the if-clause: "applications ... ______ to a senior clerk for personal review." Past and present perfect both fit; the first sentence's "has been held up" and the last sentence's present "cite" settle neither.

distractor_pulls.have been routed: Right number, and the present perfect continues the first sentence's frame ("has been held up") and is the register for an agency's standing practice; the condition sits before the subject, so by the blank the reader has stopped tracking its tense.
distractor_pulls.was routed: "employer" stands right before the blank, and the sentence is about how one employer was treated.
distractor_pulls.has been routed: The opening sentence fixes a singular present perfect about one office ("has been held up"); a reader carrying that frame onto one employer's file writes "has been routed".

distractor_kills.have been routed: Tense sequence: a habitual past condition ("reached") needs a past main verb. Correct in: "If outdated forms reach the desk, applications have been routed ..." is still odd; correct in: "Applications have been routed to a clerk this year."
distractor_kills.was routed: Subject-verb agreement: the head is plural "applications". Correct in: "the application from the employer was routed".
distractor_kills.has been routed: Wrong on number and aspect. Correct in: "The application has been routed to a clerk."

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: Two 'been', two simple pasts; no extra word.
heuristics_that_give_key: (e) 'been' loses: yes - batch-level tell named by readers; the row fixes a non-perfect key
hostile_reader.changed: Revision: the decider moved from a trailing if-clause to a FRONTED if-clause before the subject, so nothing after the blank decides; the head is no longer the sentence's first word.

frame: Opening phrase "Under the harbor commission's charter," (singular), plural subject "berth assignments for the town's fishing crews" + the blank; unless-clause whose finite verb "voted" is delayed by a participial interrupter
decider_quote: voted to make the arrangement permanent
deletion_test: Delete the unless-clause: "berth assignments ... ______ provisional." The following sentence is a general present ("argue", "discourage", "cannot"), so nothing settles past against present perfect.

distractor_pulls.have been provisional: Right number; "unless the full council, meeting each spring" reads as a standing rule in the present ("meeting" carries no tense), and the passage's other sentence is present, so the perfect looks like the ongoing-arrangement form until "voted" arrives twelve words on.
distractor_pulls.was provisional: The sentence opens on the singular "the harbor commission's charter", which looks like the thing that "was provisional".
distractor_pulls.has been provisional: The condition renames the subject as the singular "the arrangement"; a reader maps it back ("the arrangement has been provisional"), helped by the standing-rule reading.

distractor_kills.have been provisional: Tense sequence: a habitual condition in the past ("voted") needs a past main verb. Correct in: "... have been provisional unless the council has voted to extend them."
distractor_kills.was provisional: Subject-verb agreement: the subject is plural "ceilings"; "authority" is the object of "For". Correct in: "For the authority, the cap was provisional ...".
distractor_kills.has been provisional: Wrong on number (plural "ceilings") and on aspect (past condition). Correct in: "The cap has been provisional unless the council has renewed it."

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: Two 'been' forms, two simple pasts; shared 'provisional'.
heuristics_that_give_key: (e) 'been' loses: yes (row-fixed non-perfect key; batch-level tell)
hostile_reader.changed: Revision: the deciding past verb moved from word 5 to word 12 behind a tenseless participial interrupter ("meeting each spring ..."); the condition now names the singular "arrangement" (no plural pronoun); new opening phrase, subject and topic. The decider stays after the blank as the row requires, unlike D4, whose condition is now fronted.

frame: Clause 1 "Field linguists who worked in the valley left hundreds of reel-to-reel tapes in a single trunk at a regional museum" (plural object = antecedent, inside a singular container), ", so" + "the museum's archivist" + the blank
deletion_test: Delete "hundreds of reel-to-reel tapes" ("left [something] in a single trunk"): nothing named is the material being converted, so it/them is unsettled; the trunk itself is not convertible.

distractor_pulls.are converting it: "are" is pulled by the plural cast of clause 1 ("Field linguists", "tapes"), and "it" by "a single trunk", the singular holder of everything that was left.
distractor_pulls.is converting it: The verb is right, and "it" picks up "a single trunk" (the deposit as one unit) or the singular "catalog" after the blank.
distractor_pulls.are converting them: "them" is right, and the plural verb matches the plural noun it points to; the linguists are the people doing work in clause 1.

distractor_kills.are converting it: Wrong on both: singular "archivist" needs "is"; "tapes" needs "them". Correct in: "the archivists are converting it [one tape]".
distractor_kills.is converting it: Pronoun-antecedent: the material converted into digital files is the tapes; a trunk is a container and the catalog is the destination. Correct in: "left one tape ..., so the archivist is converting it".
distractor_kills.are converting them: Subject-verb: the subject is the singular "archivist". Correct in: "the museum's archivists are converting them".

heuristics_that_give_key: (f) opposite verb/pronoun numbers: YES - table-level tell
hostile_reader.changed: Revision: removed "sole" and "one cassette at a time" (both signposted the answer); the antecedent now sits inside a singular container ("a single trunk"), giving "it" a real but wrong referent; new verb.

frame: Clause 1 "Within a few months, borrowers in the district had switched to paying by text message" (plural owner), ", but" + singular subject "the lender's only bookkeeper" + appositive "a former schoolteacher with little faith in the new technology," + the blank
deletion_test: Delete "borrowers in the district": no noun in the passage has names and amounts to record ("economists" audit, they do not pay), so its/their is unsettled.

distractor_pulls.were entering its: "were" is pulled by the plural cast of clause 1 ("borrowers", "months") across a long appositive that hides the subject, and "its" by the singular "technology" right before the blank.
distractor_pulls.was entering its: The verb is right, and "its" picks up the singular "technology" (or "the lender") immediately before the blank, the nearest non-person noun a possessive can refer to.
distractor_pulls.were entering their: "their" is right, and after a 12-word appositive a reader who has lost the singular subject matches the verb to the plural owner, keeping verb and pronoun together.

distractor_kills.were entering its: Wrong on both: the subject is singular "bookkeeper"; names and amounts belong to the borrowers.
distractor_kills.was entering its: Pronoun-antecedent: names and payment amounts are the borrowers'; a technology and a lender have none to enter. Correct in: "the lender was publishing its rates".
distractor_kills.were entering their: Subject-verb: the subject is the singular "bookkeeper"; the appositive does not change its number. Correct in: "the lender's two bookkeepers were entering their names".

heuristics_that_give_key: (f) opposite verb/pronoun numbers: YES - table-level tell
hostile_reader.changed: Revision for exclusivity: the possessed noun is now "names and amounts", which no singular noun in the sentence can own (v1's "repayments" could be read as the office's repayments). Architecture: a 12-word appositive now separates subject and verb, and no institution noun precedes the blank as a possible owner.

frame: "agree that the ______ plans for a riverfront stadium kept the site idle": with no apostrophe, "the mayor plans for ..." reads as a complete that-clause until "kept"; the owner count comes only from "voters never changed mayors" in the first sentence
structure: The blank is the possessive determiner of "plans" inside a that-clause. Sentence 2 alone allows mayor's or mayors'; sentence 1's "never changed mayors" (one mayor throughout) decides.

distractor_pulls.mayors': The first sentence itself prints "mayors", and a twelve-year span suggests several administrations; a reader who skims "changed mayors" as "went through mayors" picks the plural possessive.
distractor_pulls.mayor: After "agree that", "the mayor plans for a riverfront stadium" is a perfectly formed clause (subject + verb + phrase), so the no-apostrophe form reads fluently until "kept".
distractor_pulls.mayors: It matches the spelling the passage already uses ("changed mayors"), and a reader who has settled on 'several mayors' copies it without checking the apostrophe.

distractor_kills.mayors': Plural possessive implies several owners; "voters never changed mayors" means one mayor served the whole time.
distractor_kills.mayor: If "plans" is the verb, "kept the site idle" has no subject; the owner of the noun "plans" needs the possessive.
distractor_kills.mayors: A plural without an apostrophe cannot own "plans", and as subject it disagrees with the verb reading "plans".

hostile_reader.options_only_pick: 'mayors' may be struck at a glance; 'mayor' now survives a surface read because "the mayor plans for ..." forms a clause after "agree that".
heuristics_that_give_key: the count is no longer stated as a number (no 'single'/'one'); it must be inferred from the idiom 'never changed mayors'
hostile_reader.changed: Revision: removed "a single mayor" (stated the count outright); the deciding sentence now implies one mayor through an idiom that itself contains the lure "mayors"; the blank now sits in a that-clause where the no-apostrophe form garden-paths.
